- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Gives MoE layers of an inference-optimized MLA model their pre-MLP norm.

**Bug.** #3496 added MoE support to `get_gpt_layer_with_inference_submodules`, with a pre-MLP norm (`backend.layer_norm()`) when `num_experts` is set. Only the standard-attention branch got it. The MLA branch still sets `pre_mlp_layernorm=IdentityOp`.

A dense MLP normalizes its input inside its layer-norm-fused `linear_fc1`, so `IdentityOp` is right there. MoE experts have no fused norm. So with `transformer_impl=inference_optimized`, every MoE layer of an MLA model (e.g. DeepSeek-V3-style) runs its router and experts on the unnormalized residual stream. No error is raised. The Transformer Engine MLA spec, which these models are trained with, has the norm.

**Fix.** The inference spec now chooses the pre-MLP norm once, before it branches on the attention type, so the MLA and standard-attention layers share one rule and cannot drift apart again. The norm is declared with `has_residual=True`, like the MLA input norm and the Transformer Engine spec. That changes no module today, since the inference backend ignores `has_residual`.

**Checkpoints.** Each MLA MoE layer built from this spec now has a `pre_mlp_layernorm` module, so its state dict gains `pre_mlp_layernorm.weight` (e.g. `decoder.layers.N.pre_mlp_layernorm.weight`, plus `.bias` with LayerNorm). Checkpoints trained with the Transformer Engine MLA spec already carry this key and need no change. A checkpoint saved from an inference-optimized MLA MoE model before this PR, or a converter that emits keys from the old inference spec, lacks it, and strict dist-ckpt loading reports it as missing. Such a checkpoint never held the trained norm weights; re-export it from the training checkpoint.

**Tests.** `tests/unit_tests/models/test_gpt_layer_specs.py`:
- `test_moe_layers_normalize_the_mlp_input` checks that MoE layers get the same pre-MLP norm with and without MLA, and that dense layers get none.
- `test_norm_slots_match_the_transformer_engine_spec` checks, slot by slot, that every norm slot of the inference layer spec and of its self-attention holds a norm exactly where the Transformer Engine spec does, for MLA and standard attention, dense and MoE layers, with and without `qk_layernorm`. This guards against the inference spec diverging from the spec checkpoints are trained with.

Both are spec-only (no kernel runs) and skip without Transformer Engine. On `main`, the MLA MoE cases fail (3 of 10); with this PR all pass.

On H100 in the CI image, `test_moe_layers_normalize_the_mlp_input` fails on `main` (1 case, MLA) and passes with this PR (2 cases); the neighbor test `tests/unit_tests/models/test_moe_module_specs.py` passes (4 cases). With the review changes (dfw 21004395), `test_gpt_layer_specs.py` passes 10 cases with this PR and fails 3 on `main`, exactly the MLA MoE cases; the neighbor test passes (4 cases). The 57-task inference-vs-training matrix passes on integration trees of current `main` with every open fix (dfw 21004395, 21007036).

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none; this PR's regression tests reproduce the bug.

## Code provenance

No external code was copied or adapted.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation

@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+# Copyright (c) 2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION. All rights reserved.
+
+"""Tests of the GPT layer specs."""
+
+import dataclasses
+
+import pytest
+
+from megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine import HAVE_TE
+from megatron.core.models.gpt.gpt_layer_specs import (
+    get_gpt_layer_with_inference_submodules,
+    get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_submodules,
+)
+from megatron.core.transformer.identity_op import IdentityOp
+
+
+def _norm_slots(submodules):
+    """Which norm slots of a layer and of its self-attention hold a norm."""
+    attention = submodules.self_attention.submodules
+    return {
+        f"{prefix}{field.name}": getattr(owner, field.name) not in (None, IdentityOp)
+        for prefix, owner in (("", submodules), ("self_attention.", attention))
+        for field in dataclasses.fields(owner)
+        if field.name.endswith("layernorm")
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not HAVE_TE, reason="the inference-optimized spec requires Transformer Engine")
+class TestInferenceLayerSpec:
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("multi_latent_attention", [False, True])
+    def test_moe_layers_normalize_the_mlp_input(self, multi_latent_attention):
+        """A dense MLP normalizes its input inside linear_fc1, but MoE experts do not, so a MoE
+        layer needs its own pre-MLP norm, with MLA as with standard attention."""
+        dense = get_gpt_layer_with_inference_submodules(
+            multi_latent_attention=multi_latent_attention
+        )
+        moe = get_gpt_layer_with_inference_submodules(
+            multi_latent_attention=multi_latent_attention, num_experts=8
+        )
+        assert dense.pre_mlp_layernorm is IdentityOp
+        assert moe.pre_mlp_layernorm is not IdentityOp
+        assert (
+            moe.pre_mlp_layernorm
+            == get_gpt_layer_with_inference_submodules(num_experts=8).pre_mlp_layernorm
+        )
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("qk_layernorm", [False, True])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("num_experts", [None, 8])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("multi_latent_attention", [False, True])
+    def test_norm_slots_match_the_transformer_engine_spec(
+        self, multi_latent_attention, num_experts, qk_layernorm
+    ):
+        """Checkpoints are trained with the Transformer Engine spec, so the inference spec must
+        normalize in the same places: each norm slot holds a norm in both specs or in neither."""
+        kwargs = dict(
+            multi_latent_attention=multi_latent_attention,
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            qk_layernorm=qk_layernorm,
+        )
+        assert _norm_slots(get_gpt_layer_with_inference_submodules(**kwargs)) == _norm_slots(
+            get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_submodules(**kwargs)
+        )
